findings.reason: The quotient model, incidence embedding and Springer projection are distinct interfaces in step 1.2. A restriction square alongside the projection square makes the singleton-fiber scope of step 3.1 explicit and materially clarifies how these interfaces fit together. The complete existing proof does not remove this explanatory value. All three original screenshot tiles were inspected at original resolution.

correction: Added the open-orbit restriction square and incidence-projection square in final Remarks, with quotient well-definedness, map definitions and precise fiber-scope explanation. Original title, full frontmatter, Statement, Facts and proof remain byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.justification: Fact F4 identifies T*X with G times^B n+. Under (g,x)~(gb,Ad(b^-1)x), gbB=gB and Ad(gb)Ad(b^-1)x=Ad(g)x. Hence the incidence identification used in step 1.2 descends to the quotient. Its image is I because y=Ad(g)x exactly when x=Ad(g^-1)y belongs to n+.

i maps I into X times N and pr2 maps X times N to N. Under T*X congruent I, pr2 i sends [g,x] to Ad(g)x, exactly mu in step 1.2. The bottom N=N arrow is equality. Thus the two paths from T*X to N agree; neither mu nor i is labeled an isomorphism onto N or X times N.

O=G.e is open in N by step 1.1; mu^-1(O) is its open inverse image in T*X. Horizontal hooks are inclusions; mu_O is the restriction defined in step 3.1. Inclusion after mu_O agrees with mu after inclusion by definition of inverse image and restriction.

Singleton geometric fibers are attached only to mu_O, as proved in step 3.1. Nothing asserts singleton boundary fibers or that mu is globally an isomorphism. Properness is attributed to closed I in X times N and projective X, precisely step 1.2/F4; birationality is only the already established conclusion of step 3.1.
pr1 i has codomain X and sends [g,x] to gB, the bundle projection for the associated-bundle model in F4; it is distinguished from the N-valued mu.
